title: How Sónar plans to reclaim the ‘essence’ of its electronic legacy
summary: After declaring the Sónar brand “dead” on social media last week, the Spanish electronic music institution is plotting a forward-looking return to form in 2027, CEO François Jozic tells IQ. The festival will return for its 34th edition from 17-19 June, with the Sónar by Day programme returning to its central Barcelona location after a year away. title: ‘Enduring demand’ for live pushes royalties to record €1.4bn
summary: In 2025, global royalties for music creators grew nearly 12% to a record €14.06 billion, driven in part by the rapidly growing live performance segment, according to the latest Global Collections Report. Issued by the International Confederation of Societies of Authors and Composers (CISAC), the comprehensive report compiles findings from 228 authors’ societies in 111 countries and territories, spanning music, audiovisual, visual arts, literature, and drama. title: Martin Garrix plots ‘biggest ever’ India tour with ten-date run
summary: Dutch DJ Martin Garrix has announced a ten-date tour of India to take place in March 2027, with production partner Sunburn Festival promising “the biggest tour India has ever seen”. title: BTS to livestream two ‘Arirang’ shows to thousands of cinemas
summary: BTS will livestream two upcoming stadium concerts, including the closing performance of the Asian leg of their blockbuster Arirang tour in Jakarta, to 2,800 cinemas worldwide. title: Fans hospitalised after stand collapses at Red Hot Summer Tour
summary: Three people were hospitalised and 22 treated for injuries after the collapse of a bandstand at Red Hot Summer tour in Australia’s Gold Coast. The stand collapsed at the event’s Coolangatta Beach venue site during a performance by the band Boom Crash Opera. The festival resumed later with sets from other acts, including Men At Work and Australian Crawl, though Boom Crash Opera did not finish their performance. title: Report: 94% of disabled audiences put at risk at live events
summary: Ninety-four percent of disabled audiences in the UK expose themselves to risk when attending live music and live events, according to a new report, underscoring ongoing accessibility hurdles in the industry. This is according to Access is Everything’s State of Access report, the UK disabled-led accessibility charity’s first major report in eight years and first since the pandemic. title: Australian live bodies launch nationwide venue map for tour planning
summary: Australian live music industry organisations have launched a free-to-use national venue directory which aims to let agents and artists plan tours with its interactive tools. title: Francophone music ‘a growing sensation’ after largest ever UK show
summary: After Congolese artist Fally Ipupa set a record for the largest Francophone concert in UK history, the artist’s representative says French-language music is “finally getting attention” internationally. After two consecutive nights at The O2 on 24 and 25 October, Rob Hallett, who represented Ipupa for the London dates, says the appetite for Congolese music has reached the point of supporting a run of European festival slots for Ipupa. “It’s a growing sensation. Francophone music is finally getting attention,” he tells IQ.
